_meta.description: Gene-level (WGS-confirmed) resistance evidence from Jimma Medical Center, Ethiopia - the same research group's E. coli and K. pneumoniae genomic epidemiology studies. Unlike the other Ethiopia seed files (phenotypic susceptibility testing only), these records name the specific resistance gene/allele, which is what the Mechanisms/AlphaFold feature needs to connect real evidence to a protein structure.

sources.source_title: Polyclonal spread of blaCTX-M-15 through high-risk clones of Escherichia coli at a tertiary hospital in Ethiopia
sources.source_authors: Sewunet T, Asrat D, Woldeamanuel Y, Ny S, Westerlund F, Aseffa A, Giske CG
sources.source_institution: Jimma Medical Center, Ethiopia; Addis Ababa University; Karolinska Institutet
sources.source_license: unknown - check publisher terms before redistributing full text; percentages here are cited facts, not reproduced text
sources.note: Whole-genome sequencing (Illumina HiSeq2500) of E. coli isolates from clinical specimens. ESBL-EC prevalence was 54.8% (143/261) of all E. coli; gene-level results below are among the WGS-analyzed ESBL-EC subset (n=138).

sources.source_title: High prevalence of blaCTX-M-15 and nosocomial transmission of hypervirulent epidemic clones of Klebsiella pneumoniae at a tertiary hospital in Ethiopia
sources.source_authors: Sewunet T, Asrat D, Woldeamanuel Y, Ny S, Westerlund F, Aseffa A, Giske CG
sources.source_institution: Jimma Medical Center, Ethiopia; Addis Ababa University; Karolinska Institutet
sources.source_license: CC BY-NC (Oxford Academic open access) - non-commercial use only, same caution as the other NC-licensed source in this project
sources.note: Whole-genome sequencing of all ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae isolates (n=109 successfully sequenced of 111 ESBL-KP). ESBL-KP prevalence was 76% (111/146) of all K. pneumoniae isolated; gene-level results below are among the WGS-analyzed subset (n=109). Specimens: sputum, wound swab, urine, stool from medical/surgical/paediatric/ICU units.

records.note: 122/138 WGS-analyzed ESBL-producing E. coli isolates carried blaCTX-M-15 - the dominant ESBL gene, spread across international high-risk clones ST131, ST410, ST648, ST167.
92/109 WGS-analyzed ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae isolates carried blaCTX-M-15 - the predominant ESBL gene, associated with high-risk clone ST15 (also encoding blaSHV-28).
2/109 isolates - very small count, one of which co-carried blaCTX-M-15 in the same strain.

Only 1 of 109 WGS-analyzed ESBL-KP strains carried a carbapenemase gene (blaNDM-1), despite 33/111 (22.6%) showing phenotypic carbapenem non-susceptibility - a real gap between phenotype and this specific genotype worth keeping visible, not smoothing over. This strain was also hypervirulent (ST45) and carried a broad-range IncA/C2 plasmid. NOTE: this evidence record is independent of whether NDM-1's AlphaFold structure mapping is verified - see data/reference/resistance_genes.json, where NDM-1 is still marked unverified for that separate reason.
